title: engineering-town-hall-roadmap-checkin-may-2026
content:
Engineering Town Hall — Roadmap Check-in (May 14, 2026)

Attendees: Maya Rodriguez (host), Liam Chen, Aisha Gomez, Noah Patel, Ruth Kim + ~70 engineers (cross-org). Quick notes, decisions, and action items. This doc is a sketch of the session and the follow-ups; it intentionally captures chat fragments and ‘notes-to-self’ style items.

Agenda:
- Quick metrics snapshot (2 min)
- Major program updates: Serving Runtime, Dedicated capacity, Private (VPC) deployments, Console + Rollouts (10 min)
- Incidents and reliability (5 min)
- Roadmap highlights & tradeoffs for Q2 finish and Q3 planning (20 min)
- Open Q&A and parking lot (15 min)

Metrics snapshot (presented by Aisha):
- Host API p50 generation latency: 42ms (global), p95: 210ms; down 6% p50 vs. Apr week avg.
- Dedicated cluster utilization: 78% avg; peak 95% on Monday (eu-west region).
- Token throughput (hosted): 3.1B tokens/day (up 12% w/w).
- Cost per 1M tokens (weighted): ~$8.40 (improvement due to caching + batch tuning).
- Error budget burn rate: 0.9% this sprint.

Major updates by area:
1) Serving Runtime (Liam)
- Kernel selector v0.9 deployed to staging; observed ~18% p50 token generation improvement for longer seqs (1k+ tokens).
- KV-cache prefetch experiment (infra/serving-runtime) rolled to 20% traffic; early results: 27% fewer redundant KV ops, memory pressure manageable.
- Next: finalize kernel-selector fallback logic (PLAT-2890) before prod push. Target: 2026-05-21.
- Risks: some older models (legacy quantized variants) still showing model-compatibility regressions under kernel swaps — tracking in INF-3421.

2) Dedicated (Noah)
- Autoscale smoothing landed; reduces oscillation for workloads with spiky prewarm patterns.
- New reserve booking flow in Console (beta) — onboarding for two pilot customers next week.
- Capacity planning: EU-west needs a small burst allocation for May 27–31. Action: Ops to approve temporary burst capacity; cost estimate attached in Confluence.

3) Private Deployments & Security (Ruth)
- Private package 1.3.0 candidate submitted; includes KMS integration for AWS/GCP and improved audit log format.
- On-prem installer script bugs: installer.sh emits incorrect SELinux context on RHEL 8. Patch MR opened — aiming for hotfix release 1.3.1 by 2026-05-20.
- Compliance ask: CISO requested a short runbook for offline upgrades in air-gapped installs — Ruth + Solutions Eng to draft by 2026-05-19.

4) Console & Rollouts (Maya)
- Rollout groups UI mock reviewed; A/B and canary toggles are in design review.
- Tracing hooks: backend change to surface per-request token cost in the trace span. Need one more data point from serving runtime team about overhead.

Incidents and reliability (brief)
- Incident recap (May 3): external dependency (third-party metrics ingestion) caused a 45 min spike in error rates for hosted API. Lessons: better RBAC/timeout defaults for ingestion clients; added default backoff to metrics agent.
- Follow-up: SRE to propose a small runbook to handle similar external ingestion failures. Owner: Priya (SRE). ETA: 2026-05-18.

Roadmap guidance and tradeoffs (discussion notes)
- Tradeoff: aggressive kernel-selector rollout (performance wins) vs. model-compatibility risk on legacy quantized variants. Decision: continue canary with narrower slice (priority: high-latency long-seq traffic), extend monitoring windows, and keep a human-in-loop rollback for first 48 hours of wide rollout.
- Prioritization ask from Sales: faster Availability SLAs for Dedicated customers. Discussed resource trade: commit incremental ops headcount vs. automated failover work. Outcome: short term — prioritize automation for failover (engineering effort) and propose a staffed on-call augmentation as a Q3 contract option.

Q&A highlights
Q: "When will we expose better per-route cost breakdowns in the public dashboard?" — Answer: Console team aiming for an initial beta (token-level cost per route) by end of June; depends on the trace-span token cost change landing.
Q: "Is there a plan to reduce p95 latency spikes for small prompt patterns?" — SRE + Serving to run a focused experiment on micro-batching thresholds; results due 2026-05-25.
Q: "Private deployments: any ETA for Windows support?" — Not prioritized; on roadmap for exploratory research in Q3.

Decisions and action items (concrete)
- PLAT-2890: kernel-selector fallback logic — Owner: Liam; Due: 2026-05-21.
- INF-3421: compatibility regression triage for legacy quantized models — Owner: Aisha; Due: 2026-05-20.
- On-prem installer SELinux hotfix (1.3.1) — Owner: Ruth; Due: 2026-05-20.
- Burst capacity approval (EU-west May 27–31) — Owner: Ops (cc: Noah); Due: 2026-05-18.
- Runbook for external metrics ingestion failure — Owner: Priya (SRE); Due: 2026-05-18.
- Console trace span token-cost change: collect perf overhead data — Owner: Liam + Console eng; Due: 2026-05-19.

Parking lot (items to capture for future discussions)
- Deeper look at prefetch cache eviction heuristics (serving runtime R&D).
- Long-term: unified observability schema across Hosted/Dedicated/Private for cost attribution.
- On-call rotation compensation and hiring plan (people ops + eng leads).

Shoutouts
- Thanks to the infra team for the recent autoscale smoothing rollout (Noah noted a visible reduction in oscillation for two pilot workloads).
- Congrats to the serving-runtime team for the kernel-selector perf gains in staging.

Notes-to-self / loose fragments captured in chat:
- "Need a short blurb for customer comms about kernel-selector safety nets" — Maya
- "Quantized regressions: gather a set of failing prompts and tie to eval harness so we can alert regressions automatically" — Aisha
- "Add a checkbox to release checklist: verify trace-span size growth when adding instrumentation" — Ruth

Next steps / follow-up meeting
- Roadmap deep-dive (60m) scheduled for 2026-05-21, invites sent to eng leads and product partners.
- Weekly sync cadence remains Tuesdays 11:00 PT for cross-org open floor.

If you want to flag anything missing or add items to the parking lot, reply in the town-hall thread or add a comment on the Confluence page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ENG-TOWN-HALL-2026-05-14

End notes: This doc is a working capture; we'll iterate and mark as final after owners update Jira tickets and Confluence artifacts.

-- Maya
